gaps: No support surface. In workyard-LOD0, 14/14 pestle footprints are NO_SUPPORT (126/126 downward rays miss) and the yard has no floor at all; probe at (0,0) hits nothing. The standalone pestle also has no ground, with all 14 footprints at z=0.

The baked install is not withdrawable. In workyard only the lever is a separate node; static timber is merged into workyard_timber and the mortar into workyard_stone. Installing the standalone pestle at the same T double-loads 21/21 components (doubleLoad FAIL).

Pivot hole is open but there is no contact support. Lever hole r=0.079 (16/16 probes) vs axle r=0.075, with axle-lever overlap 0 m3. The post saddle bottom is at z=0.921 and the axle bottom at 0.925, so the moving parts and axle hang on 4 mm gaps.
8 deg pose has about 3 mm margin. The lever hits the platform at about 8.13 deg: lever min z 0.723 vs platform 0.720 at 8 deg, and overlap is 5.6e-5 m3 at 8.5 deg.
Pestle hangs 5 cm above the bowl at 0 deg (pestle z=0.35, bowl bottom 0.30). Bowl contact is at about -2.1 deg, outside the allowed poses [0,4,8]. Stroke is 0.175 m over 0-8 deg.

Platform is 1.25x1.20 m at 0.72 m with 3 risers of 0.24 m and 0.35 m treads. Rails give 1.19 m clear width and stand 0.985 m above the platform. The lever splits the platform into two 0.485 m strips plus a lever-free 1.19x0.40 m front zone, so a 0.6 m turning circle does not fit. The back edge has no rail and drops 0.72 m.

Inherited static embeds: pivot post fully through base 0.0088 m3 x2; rail post into platform about 3e-4 m3 x4; rail post into step 9e-5 m3 x2; rail top into post 2.1e-4 m3 x4; pestle tenon into lever 2.75e-3 m3.

Axis convention: workyard pivot_m [5,-1.5,1.2] is in Blender Z-up, not glTF. The standalone moving node has no pivot extras and its origin is not at the axle, at local (0,0,1.0) Blender / (0,1.0,0) glTF.
LOD2 has no moving node (static only). There is also a 1 cm datum mismatch: workyard base is 0.20 while city ground top is 0.21.

Alternative host workshed-LOD0 has no floor either. With the pestle centred in the right bay (T=1.55,2.0,0), support is FAIL with 14/14 NO_SUPPORT. Other results there: plan gap to posts 0.745 m each side; headroom over the platform 2.45-2.88 m; no horizontal ray hits; doubleLoad PASS. The pestle is 4.21 m long against 3.5 m between post rows, so the step front pokes out to the eave line at y≈-0.45.
reuseCandidate: Partial reuse. The pestle geometry can be reused unchanged: compare_runs shows 21/21 components match with deviation <1 mm between standalone LOD0 and workyard, and LOD1/2 differ only in rails, ≤7.4 mm. The workyard install (T=(5,-1.5,0.2), poses 0/4/8) is a C reference. It does not qualify as the deliverable, because it has no floor (NO_SUPPORT 14/14), cannot be withdrawn (baked), and is not admitted to the city. No new pestle geometry is needed, only the assembly package plus ground interface.

risks: LY-010 may choose no admitted work site. In that case the package stays an independent demo domain and cannot count as 已入城.
If the ground contract lacks a flat patch of at least 1.41x4.21 m plus an approach zone, a pad or cut is required, and its ownership with LY-006 or the ground owner may conflict.
With only 3 mm margin at 8 deg, any pad, mat or platform finish layer would make the treadle collide. Attachments must stay out of the lever sweep and the pivot envelope.
The 0 deg rest pose is visually a hanging pestle (5 cm gap). Changing the pose table touches the moving-semantics owner, so it must not be altered silently.
Blender-axis pivot_m could be misread as glTF and give a wrong runtime rotation axis.
The workyard and LY-056 install may be loaded together (double load).
Body-space numbers are geometric C envelopes, not ergonomics or safety; the unguarded back edge must be disclosed.
No original evidence on 踏碓 dimensions at Luoyang c.180: all dims are C, and Sichuan bricks, Northern Wei or Western Han material cannot be imported as fact.
